title: BurnSig – Early detection of sepsis in severely burned patients by identifying a biomarker signature after machine-learning-based risk stratification
summary: After severe burns, the body mounts a strong inflammatory response that closely resembles blood poisoning (sepsis), so sepsis is often recognised late. A computer model developed at our clinic identifies patients at high sepsis risk on admission, but it also raises an alarm for many patients who never develop sepsis. In this study, adult high-risk burn patients in intensive care give a small daily blood sample (up to 10 ml, at most 140 ml in total) for up to 14 days, usually from an existing catheter. Inflammatory proteins are measured in these samples, including pancreatic stone protein (PSP). The aim is a combination of blood markers that detects developing sepsis earlier and more reliably. Treatment is not changed by the study.

interventions.name: Sepsis group: patients classified as high risk by the AI model who develop sepsis during the course (Sepsis-3 criteria, ABA criteria, expert judgement). Daily serum sample (up to 10 ml) for up to 14 days and an additional sample at clinical sepsis diagnosis.

Control group: patients classified as high risk by the AI model who do not develop sepsis (false positives). Sampling identical to the sepsis group. Group assignment is made retrospectively from the clinical course.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age 18 years or older
- Severe burn injury (usually more than 15% TBSA) requiring intensive care treatment
- Classified as high risk by the group's AI early-warning model applied at admission
- Written informed consent of the patient or legal representative; patients who regain capacity are asked for their own consent, and participation ends if they decline
Exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing clinically relevant anaemia or other conditions in which additional blood sampling would pose a risk to the course of treatment
